extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders (manufacturers, industry groups, consumer groups, attorneys, and other commenters) who may submit comments on NHTSA proposed rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural requirements for preparing, formatting, submitting, and protecting comments (including confidential business information) in response to an NHTSA proposed rule; includes deadline, docket reference, and public availability rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments must be written and in English. To ensure that your comments are correctly filed in the Docket, please include the docket number indicated in this document in your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the docket number and the date and page number of this issue of the Federal Register when submitting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limit for primary comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments must not be more than 15 pages long. (49 CFR 553.21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 15-page limit is intended to encourage concise primary comments; however, you may attach necessary additional documents to your comments. There is no limit on the length of attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic PDF formatting (OCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are submitting comments electronically as a PDF (Adobe) file, NHTSA asks that the documents be submitted using the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR allows NHTSA to search and copy portions of your submissions. Ensure electronic files are searchable text when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality for substantive data
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Data Quality Act, in order for substantive data to be relied upon and used by the agency, it must meet the information quality standards set forth in the OMB and DOT Data Quality Act guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the OMB and DOT information-dissemination/data quality guidelines when preparing substantive data; OMB's guidelines may be accessed at the DOT link provided in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to ensure the docket received your mailed comment
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish the Docket to notify you upon its receipt of your comments, enclose a self-addressed, stamped postcard in the envelope containing your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receiving your comments, the Docket will return the postcard by mail as confirmation of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted through the Federal rulemaking portal at http://www.regulations.gov and should reference the docket number and the date and page number of this issue of the Federal Register. NHTSA strongly prefers comments be submitted electronically. However, written comments may be submitted (i.e., postmarked) via mail to 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments submitted in response to this document will be included in the record and will be made available to the public. Any information submitted with your comment will be made public, without change, on the internet at the address provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and searchability of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments submitted will be included in the record and made available to the public on regulations.gov. Anyone is able to search the electronic form of all comments received into any of our dockets by the name of the individual submitting the comment (or signing the comment, if submitted on behalf of an association, business, labor union, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may review comments at the docket address or online at regulations.gov; the agency recommends periodically checking the docket for new material and you can arrange to be notified when others file comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential business information (CBI) submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a redacted 'public version' of your comment (including redacted versions of any additional documents or attachments) to the docket. Also submit a request for confidential treatment directly to the Office of Chief Counsel. Your request must set forth the information specified in part 512.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are required to submit to the Office of Chief Counsel one unredacted 'confidential version' of the information for which you are seeking confidential treatment and one redacted 'public version' for the docket. Follow 49 CFR part 512 (including §§512.4(b), 512.5(a)(2), 512.6, 512.8 and part 512, appendix A) for required content and certifications. NHTSA currently accepts electronic submission for CBI requests; do not send a hardcopy. Send the request to Daniel.Rabinovitz@dot.gov or request a secure file transfer link, and email a courtesy copy to John.Piazza@dot.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking pages with confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to §512.6, the words 'ENTIRE PAGE CONFIDENTIAL BUSINESS INFORMATION' or 'CONFIDENTIAL BUSINESS INFORMATION CONTAINED WITHIN BRACKETS' (as applicable) must appear at the top of each page containing information claimed to be confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not all information on the page is claimed confidential, identify each item of information for which confidentiality is requested within brackets: '[ ].' The redacted public version should include only the portions for which no claim of confidential treatment is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency consideration of late comments
rubrics_metrics.description: We will consider all comments received before the close of business on the comment closing date indicated above under DATES. To the extent possible, we will also consider comments that the docket receives after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the docket receives a comment too late for us to consider in developing a final rule (assuming one is issued), we will consider that comment as an informal suggestion for future rulemaking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for comments (specific rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received within 60 days of May 30, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this deadline when planning submission; late submissions may be considered as described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language guidance for commenters
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of the principles of plain language includes consideration of the following questions: Have we organized the material to suit the public's needs? Are the requirements in the rule clearly stated? Does the rule contain technical language or jargon that isn't clear? Would a different format (grouping and order of sections, use of headings, paragraphing) make the rule easier to understand? Would more (but shorter) sections be better? Could we improve clarity by adding tables, lists, or diagrams? What else could we do to make the rule easier to understand?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have any responses to these questions, please include them in your comments on this proposal. Use plain-language organization and formatting to improve clarity and usefulness of your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text change — S5.1.1 (GVWR ≤ 10,000 lbs.)
rubrics_metrics.description: S5.1.1 Vehicles with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or less. Each passenger car, multipurpose passenger vehicle, truck, and bus with a GVWR of 10,000 pounds or less that uses CNG as a motor fuel shall meet the requirements of S6, except S6.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the proposed regulatory requirement as amended in §571.303; comments may address technical or draftsmanship issues relating to this text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory text change — S5.1.2 (school buses > 10,000 lbs.)
rubrics_metrics.description: S5.1.2 School buses with a GVWR greater than 10,000 pounds. Each school bus with a GVWR greater than 10,000 pounds that uses CNG as a motor fuel shall meet the requirements of S6.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the proposed regulatory requirement as amended in §571.303; commenters may address impacts, applicability, or clarity of this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act / identification optionality
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT posts comments, without edit, to www.regulations.gov, as described in the system of records notice, DOT/ALL-14 FDMS. In order to facilitate comment tracking and response, we encourage commenters to provide their name, or the name of their organization; however, submission of names is completely optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that provided identifying information will be publicly searchable with comments; consult DOT's Privacy Act Statement referenced in the notice for details.
